statement: Stop blocked rather than pick one of the two conflicting team decisions for the 0-balance sweep; no change to src/Ledger or tests, because any sweep implementation must choose a behaviour for the 0-balance case and so would silently override one team's recorded decision.

Added StandingOrder, OrderOutcome and LedgerError.InvalidOrder to Domain.fs exactly as specified; StandingOrders.fs is compiled between Ledger.fs and Store.fs so it can use Ledger.transfer/setDate. No Store wrapper was added (not required).

Validation runs over the whole list before the date check; OrderId duplicates are detected with ordinal (Set<string>) equality; Error (InvalidOrder id) names the first offending order. The date check and the business-date move reuse Ledger.setDate, so a past date yields DateInPast and payments are stamped with the new date.

Paid in full or not at all: each due order is a single Ledger.transfer for the full Value (which refuses with InsufficientFunds rather than paying part); a refused transfer becomes Skipped(id, error) and the run continues with the next order.
Due orders are sorted with String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId; the reference date is formatted yyyy-MM-dd with InvariantCulture; days in month come from DateTime.DaysInMonth.

AlreadyPaid is detected by any journal posting whose Reference equals standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd>, checked before attempting the transfer and against the state including earlier payments of the same run.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState field ClosedAccounts: Set<AccountId> (initialised empty in Ledger.empty); closeAccount moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts. Accounts keeps its type and meaning (open accounts), so every existing check (balance, credit, debit, transfer, closePeriod, Store) treats a closed id as unknown with no further change. Only Ledger.empty constructs LedgerState in the repository, so adding the field breaks no caller; existing function signatures are unchanged.

A single status map (open/closed) would make the overlap of open and closed unrepresentable but would change the type of the public Accounts field; I kept two sets and documented the invariant that they are disjoint and changed only by Ledger.openAccount/closeAccount. Code that builds a LedgerState with a record copy could still violate it.

closeAccount reuses Ledger.balance for the first check, so 'not open' (never opened or already closed) yields UnknownAccount before the balance check; any balance <> 0m (including a negative one, reachable only via a hand-built state) yields NonZeroBalance(id, balance).

openAccount refuses an id found in Accounts or ClosedAccounts with DuplicateAccount; Store.openAccount inherits this. The requirement wording 'whether or not the account ever had postings' is why reuse is not inferred from the journal.

No Store.closeAccount was added (not required). A repeated closePeriod for a period id closed before the account was closed returns the stored earlier summary, which may still list the account; I read 'a period close no longer charges or lists it' as applying to new closes, since the existing idempotency contract returns the first close's summary.

periodFee is the single definition of the fee rule; feeFor is Ledger.balance mapped through periodFee (so not-open, i.e. never opened or closed, yields UnknownAccount via balance); closePeriod charges each open account feeFor it, so preview and close cannot diverge. R1 was committed with the old rule (balance >= 1.00 pays 1.00), then R2 replaced only the body of periodFee.

Table boundaries implemented as half-open intervals: balance < 1.00 -> 0; 1.00 <= balance < 1000.00 -> 1.00; balance >= 1000.00 -> 0. A negative balance (unreachable without a hand-built state) pays 0.

closePeriod posts -fee with reference fee:<periodId> only when fee > 0; Fees still lists every open account with its fee (0 when none), and closed accounts stay unlisted as before (U3). In the fold, feeFor's Error branch defaults to 0m because every id comes from ledger.Accounts and fees never touch another account's balance; this mirrors the previous balance-defaulting code.

Idempotence unchanged: the ClosedPeriods lookup still returns the first close's summary and state untouched. No Store entry point for fees or closePeriod was added (not required; Store has none today).

Added DailyLimitExceeded of AccountId * decimal as the last LedgerError case, as specified. Ledger.withdraw checks, in order, amount <= 0 (InvalidAmount), Ledger.balance (UnknownAccount for not open, including closed accounts), balance < amount (InsufficientFunds), then already + amount > 500.00 (DailyLimitExceeded with 500.00 - already); otherwise one posting of -amount via the existing private post helper, reference "withdraw", dated ledger.Today. Steps 1-3 mirror Ledger.debit's existing checks.

Today's withdrawn total is computed from the journal, not stored: the sum of -Amount over the account's postings (Ledger.postingsOf) with Reference = "withdraw" and Date = ledger.Today. One private helper (withdrawnOn) serves both withdraw and withdrawnToday so the limit check and the query cannot diverge. Refused withdrawals record nothing and so never count; a later business date matches no earlier postings, so the limit restarts. The limit (500m) and reference ("withdraw") are public named values dailyWithdrawalLimit and withdrawalReference.
withdrawnToday returns UnknownAccount via Ledger.balance for any account not open (never opened or closed), consistent with feeFor; it returns 0 when there are no withdrawals today.

The reference "withdraw" is not reserved: debit/credit/transfer still accept it, so a debit with reference "withdraw" would count as a withdrawal (the requirement defines a withdrawal as a posting with that reference). Reserving it would add a new refusal to existing operations, which V8 does not ask for; this follows the precedent of unreserved standing-order references.
No Store.withdraw entry point added (not required; Store has no entry point for closeAccount or closePeriod either).

Added InvalidCount of int as the last LedgerError case, as specified, and Ledger.richest with the specified signature. A negative count is checked first and refused with InvalidCount carrying the count as given, even on an empty ledger.

Participants are exactly ledger.Accounts (open accounts; closed accounts are in ClosedAccounts and excluded). Each balance comes from the existing Ledger.balance (journal sum), defaulting to 0 on the unreachable UnknownAccount branch, following the closePeriod precedent; zero balances (no postings) take part.

Ordering is a single comparator: balance descending by decimal value (so 5.0 and 5.00 tie), then id ascending with String.CompareOrdinal on the id strings, made explicit rather than relying on F# generic string comparison. The sorted list is then truncated to count (List.truncate, so a larger count gives all, 0 gives []).
No Store.richest added; the requirement names only Ledger.fs, and the function is a pure read of LedgerState (Store.current gives the state).

Added BankLine and ReconciliationReport to the end of Domain.fs exactly as specified, and module Ledger.Reconciliation in src/Ledger/Reconciliation.fs, compiled right after Ledger.fs, with the specified reconcile signature. No existing public signature changed.

'Open' means ledger.Accounts contains the id; closed accounts (ClosedAccounts) and never-opened ids are refused with UnknownAccount id, the same test Ledger.balance uses. The refusal is checked before any line is examined.

The account's postings in journal order are obtained by reversing Ledger.postingsOf (newest first) and indexed by journal position; the index identifies a posting so that identical postings stay distinct, is the tie-break key, and removes a matched posting from the pool.

Match rule: Amount = Value by decimal equality (so 10.0m matches 10.00m); Reference and Memo compared with String.Equals Ordinal (exact, case-sensitive); date distance is abs of the DateOnly.DayNumber difference, <= 2 (constant Reconciliation.maxDaysApart). Selection is minBy (distance, journal index), i.e. closest date then earliest in journal order.
Numeric decimal equality for Value (scale ignored) is my reading of 'Value equals Amount'; the requirement does not address decimal scale.
No Store.reconcile added: the requirement names only Domain.fs and Reconciliation.fs, and reconcile is a pure read of LedgerState (follows U6-D4).

Holds are stored as a new LedgerState field Holds: Map<string, Hold>, keyed by hold id, with a new record Hold { HoldId; Account; Amount }. The map key makes 'at most one active hold per id' structural; releasing removes the entry, so released ids can be reused and no released-hold history is kept. Ledger.empty starts with Map.empty. DuplicateHold and UnknownHold were appended to LedgerError as specified.
Adding a field to the public LedgerState record keeps every existing function signature; the only record literal construction is Ledger.empty (tests use copy-and-update), so no caller broke.

'Not open' for available and placeHold reuses Ledger.balance (Accounts membership), so closed and never-opened accounts give UnknownAccount, consistent with U7-D2. Hold ids are compared exactly (ordinal string equality via the Map key).

debit and transfer now check Ledger.available instead of Ledger.balance at the existing InsufficientFunds step; all other refusals and their order are unchanged. StandingOrders.run (via transfer) and Store.debit/Store.transfer (delegating to Ledger) therefore respect holds without change. Holds on a transfer's destination do not matter. closePeriod/feeFor are unchanged and use the balance.

Ledger.withdraw is left unchanged: it still refuses InsufficientFunds against the balance, so a cash withdrawal can spend held money. V3-R2 names only debit and transfer, and LEDGER-V8-R1 explicitly says withdraw refuses when amount is more than the balance and 'otherwise' records the posting; making withdraw honour holds would contradict that earlier accepted requirement. Pinned by a test so a change is visible.

available is balance minus active holds without clamping, so it can be negative (e.g. after a period fee, or after a withdrawal per U8-D5). The requirement defines available as exactly that difference.
No Store.placeHold/releaseHold/available were added: the requirement names only Domain.fs and Ledger.fs (same reasoning as U7-D6). Store.create works with any state, including one carrying holds.

Stop blocked rather than pick one team's decision: any implementation of sweep must choose a zero-balance behaviour, and either choice violates a recorded decision of the other team. The two decisions are same-level records in the same file with no stated precedence, newer date or narrower scope, so the directives call for escalation, not a silent resolution.
Did not add a partial sweep implementation; src/Ledger and tests are unchanged so no contested behaviour is shipped as if agreed.

An order the payer cannot fully cover is not paid at all and is reported Skipped with the transfer's InsufficientFunds error; this is achieved by delegating to Ledger.transfer, which never moves part of an amount.
The date move reuses Ledger.setDate after order validation, so DateInPast and the date move behave exactly as setDate does, and payments are stamped with the run date through Ledger.transfer.

AlreadyPaid is detected by any posting in the journal (any account) whose Reference equals standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd>; the date is formatted with the invariant culture. Duplicate ids are refused up front, so payments within one run cannot trigger it.

A transfer refusal other than insufficient funds (unknown payer or payee, payer equal to payee) is also reported as Skipped with that error rather than refusing the run, since the requirement says any refused transfer is Skipped and only lists Value, DayOfMonth and duplicate id as InvalidOrder checks.
Ordinal ordering uses String.CompareOrdinal; the sort is stable but ids are unique after validation, so ties cannot occur.
No Store.run was added; the requirement only asks for the pure StandingOrders.run, and Store's balance cache is unaffected because Store is not involved.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState field `ClosedAccounts: Set<AccountId>`, disjoint from `Accounts`. Closing moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts. A field is needed because the requirement forbids reuse even for accounts that never had postings, so closure cannot be inferred from the journal.

Adding a record field changes LedgerState's shape (code building a LedgerState record literal must set it), but no function signature changes; the only literal in the repo is Ledger.empty, which was updated. I took 'existing public signatures kept' to mean function signatures.

closeAccount reuses Ledger.balance for both checks: an id not in Accounts gives UnknownAccount first, then any balance other than exactly 0 gives NonZeroBalance with that balance. Because balance, credit, debit, transfer and closePeriod all consult Accounts, removing the id makes them treat the account as unknown without other changes.

Added Store.closeAccount, which commits the close and removes the id from the balance cache, so the Store's rule that its cache follows every operation still holds and Store.balance reports UnknownAccount for a closed account.

Earlier period summaries stored in ClosedPeriods still list a later-closed account; they are historical records and are not rewritten. Standing orders whose payer or payee is closed are Skipped with UnknownAccount via Ledger.transfer.

periodFee is the single definition of the fee rule; feeFor is Ledger.balance mapped through periodFee, and closePeriod charges feeFor of each open account, so all three agree by construction rather than by duplicated thresholds.

closePeriod records a fee posting of minus the fee only when the fee is more than 0, and lists every open account in Fees with the fee charged (0 when none). Closed accounts are not open, so they are neither charged nor listed, as LEDGER-V1-R1 requires.

R1 and R2 were committed separately: R1 kept the old rule (verified by the existing base test and new tests; only the R2 acceptance test failed at that point), then R2 changed periodFee to the new table.

Fees no longer than the balance can never overdraw an account (the fee is at most 1.00 and only when the balance is at least 1.00), so closePeriod posts directly rather than through debit, as it did before.
Idempotence is unchanged: a stored summary for the period id is returned with the ledger untouched, regardless of the current rule; summaries from closes under the old rule are not recomputed.

Withdrawals are tallied in a new LedgerState field `Withdrawn: Map<AccountId * DateOnly, decimal>` that only Ledger.withdraw writes, instead of summing journal postings with reference "withdraw". credit, debit and transfer accept any reference string, so a debit or transfer referenced "withdraw" would otherwise count towards the limit, contradicting 'only withdrawals count (not debits, transfers or fees)'. The withdrawal itself is still the posting the requirement specifies.

Keying the tally by business date makes the limit restart when the date moves on without changing setDate; setting the same date again keeps the day's total. Old dates' entries are kept (small, and harmless since dates never move backwards).
Adding a LedgerState field again changes the record shape but no function signature; the only LedgerState literal is Ledger.empty, which was updated. Same interpretation as U3-D2.

The 500.00 limit is a private constant in Ledger.fs; DailyLimitExceeded carries 500.00 minus today's total (0 once the limit is reached). Closing an account needs no change: withdrawnToday and withdraw report UnknownAccount for it via the Accounts set.
Added Store.withdraw so the store can withdraw while keeping its balance cache in step, matching its other operations.

richest ranks every id in LedgerState.Accounts (open accounts only; closed accounts are excluded because closeAccount removes them from Accounts), with balances computed from postingsOf like Ledger.balance, sorted by balance descending then by the id string with String.CompareOrdinal, then truncated to count.

The tie-break uses an explicit String.CompareOrdinal rather than relying on F#'s structural comparison of AccountId, so the ordinal rule is visible in the code and does not depend on the union's comparison semantics.
No Store counterpart was added: richest is a read over a LedgerState and callers can use Store.current.

Postings are tracked by their position in the account's journal-order list, not by value: Posting is a value record and identical postings (same account, amount, reference and date) can occur, so value equality would match one posting twice or drop both from LedgerOnly.
The account's journal order is List.rev of Ledger.postingsOf (newest first), consistent with Ledger.postings. Open means in LedgerState.Accounts, so closed accounts are refused with UnknownAccount.

Date distance is the absolute difference of DateOnly.DayNumber, so 'at most 2 days apart' means |difference| <= 2. The tie-break to the earlier posting relies on List.minBy returning the first of equal keys over candidates kept in journal order; a test pins this.
Matching is greedy per line as specified, not a globally optimal assignment; an earlier line may take a posting a later line needed (covered by a test).

Active holds are stored in a new LedgerState field `Holds: Map<string, AccountId * decimal>` keyed by hold id (ids are unique across accounts). Releasing removes the entry, so a released id can be reused and no history of released holds is kept.

debit and transfer check `available` instead of `balance` at the InsufficientFunds step; their earlier checks and order are unchanged. Standing orders pay through transfer, so they also cannot spend held money.

withdraw (V8) also checks `available` at its InsufficientFunds step. V3-R2 names only debit and transfer, and V8-R1 says 'more than the balance', but V3-R2's governing statement is 'money that is held cannot be spent' and a cash withdrawal spends money; leaving withdraw on balance would let held money leave the account. Resolved in favour of the newer requirement; refusal order of withdraw is unchanged.

closePeriod, feeFor, richest and reconcile keep using balance; closeAccount is unchanged (it checks balance only), so an account can be closed with an active hold if its balance is 0 (possible only after a period fee takes the balance below the held amount). releaseHold still works for such a hold; available on the closed account is UnknownAccount.
Added Store.placeHold and Store.releaseHold; they update the journal state only, since holds change no balance and the store's cache holds balances.
Another LedgerState field changes the record shape but no function signature; only Ledger.empty builds a LedgerState literal. Same interpretation as U3-D2.
Stop blocked without implementing sweep, because Ordo contract admission reported a diagnostic; neither conflicting team decision was chosen over the other.

Shortfall handling follows the accepted design note: an order is paid in full via one Ledger.transfer of its whole Value, or skipped with the transfer's refusal (e.g. InsufficientFunds); no partial payment. Recorded as DEC-U2-SHORTFALL-VIA-TRANSFER.

Idempotency is derived from the journal: an order is AlreadyPaid when any posting carries reference standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd> (invariant culture); this check runs before the transfer. No paid-order state is added to LedgerState. Recorded as DEC-U2-IDEMPOTENCY-BY-REFERENCE.

run validates orders in one list-order pass (value > 0, day 1..31, id not used by an earlier order) before the date check, moves the date via Ledger.setDate, then pays due orders sorted by String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId, folding the ledger through each payment. Recorded as DEC-U2-RUN-SHAPE.

Only run is public in Ledger.StandingOrders; the reference, due-date and validation helpers are private, and Store gets no standing-order operation because none was required (DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE unaffected).
The month length for the last-day rule comes from System.DateTime.DaysInMonth, a pure calendar function, not the system clock (AR-2).

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState.ClosedAccounts set; closeAccount moves the id from Accounts (open accounts) to ClosedAccounts without recording a posting, and openAccount refuses an id in either set with DuplicateAccount. Recorded as DEC-U3-CLOSED-ACCOUNTS-SET.

Keeping Accounts as the set of open accounts means balance, credit, debit, transfer, closePeriod and StandingOrders.run treat a closed account as unknown without being changed; this relies on every one of them checking ledger.Accounts.

Adding a field to the LedgerState record is acceptable under 'existing public signatures are kept': no function signature changes, and the only construction of LedgerState in the repository is Ledger.empty.

closeAccount checks via Ledger.balance: UnknownAccount first, then any balance other than exactly 0 (negative included) is NonZeroBalance(id, balance). Store gets no close operation because none was required. Recorded as DEC-U3-CLOSE-CHECK-ORDER.
A closed account stays in the summaries of periods closed before it was closed (ClosedPeriods history is not rewritten); only later period closes omit it.

periodFee is the single definition of the fee rule; feeFor = balance mapped through periodFee, and closePeriod charges periodFee of each open account's balance. Recorded as DEC-U4-SINGLE-FEE-RULE (implements DEC-V4-SHARED-FEE-RULE).
feeFor refuses with UnknownAccount any account that is not open, including closed accounts, by reusing Ledger.balance's check.
New rule: balance >= 1.00 and < 1000.00 pays 1.00, otherwise 0 (negative balances pay 0). closePeriod posts -fee only when fee > 0 and always lists the account in Fees (0 when it paid nothing).
Periods already closed are not recalculated under the new rule; a repeated close returns the stored summary. Recorded as DEC-U4-CLOSED-PERIODS-KEEP-OLD-FEES.
R1 and R2 were done in order as separate commits; the R1 checkpoint (086a944) is expected to fail only the provided R2 acceptance test.

Withdrawals are identified in the journal by reference 'withdraw' on the account and dated with the business date; the day's total is derived from the postings, with no new LedgerState or Posting field. Recorded as DEC-U5-WITHDRAWALS-BY-REFERENCE.

withdraw refuses in the stated order (InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, InsufficientFunds via Ledger.balance, then DailyLimitExceeded(id, 500 - already) when already + amount > 500); the limit is inclusive.
withdrawnToday reports a positive total (0 when none) and refuses accounts that are not open, closed accounts included, with UnknownAccount.

The 500.00 limit and the 'withdraw' reference are private constants in Ledger.fs; only withdraw and withdrawnToday are added to the public surface. Store gets no withdraw operation because none was required (DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE unaffected).

richest ranks every open account by its derived balance, descending, ties broken by String.CompareOrdinal on the id string, then truncates to count; a negative count is refused with InvalidCount. Recorded as DEC-U6-RICHEST-RANKING.
'Open accounts' means LedgerState.Accounts, so closed accounts are left out of the ranking.
Balances are summed directly from postingsOf for each open account instead of calling Ledger.balance, to avoid an unreachable error path (an open account always has a balance).
Postings are identified by their position in the account's journal-order list, not by value, so identical postings are each matched at most once. Recorded as DEC-U7-RECONCILE-BY-POSITION.
Journal order comes from Ledger.postings (oldest first) filtered to the account, relying on the newest-first storage decision.
Each line, in order, greedily takes the unmatched candidate minimising (days apart, journal position), implementing DEC-V6-CLOSEST-FIRST; no global optimisation.
Days apart is |BookedOn.DayNumber - Date.DayNumber| <= 2; Memo/Reference compared with StringComparison.Ordinal; Value/Amount by decimal equality (so 5.0 equals 5.00).
Parameters of BankLine and Posting are type-annotated because BankLine.Value shares a label with StandingOrder.Value.
An account that is not open, closed accounts included, is refused with UnknownAccount; the postings of a closed account are therefore not reconcilable.

Active holds are stored in LedgerState.Holds: Map<string, Hold> keyed by hold id (Hold = { OnAccount; Held }); release removes the entry so the id can be reused; holds never touch postings. Recorded as DEC-U8-HOLDS-MAP.
Hold record labels (OnAccount, Held) are distinct from Posting's (Account, Amount) to avoid ambiguous F# record inference.

available = balance minus the sum of the account's active holds, and is built on balance, so it refuses accounts that are not open, closed ones included, with UnknownAccount. placeHold checks InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, DuplicateHold, then InsufficientFunds against available (a hold may take exactly the available amount).

debit and transfer (source) check InsufficientFunds against available instead of balance, at the same position in their refusal order; a hold on the destination does not limit what it receives. StandingOrders.run follows because it pays through transfer.

withdraw also checks InsufficientFunds against available, because V3 states that held money cannot be spent; with no holds, V8 behaviour is unchanged. This amends one detail of DEC-U5-WITHDRAWALS-BY-REFERENCE and is recorded as DEC-U8-SPEND-AGAINST-AVAILABLE.
closePeriod and feeFor stay on balance; a fee may therefore leave available negative while a hold is active, and the hold stays active.

closeAccount was not changed to refuse or drop active holds: V1 lists its refusals exhaustively and V3 says nothing about closing. A hold can outlive its account only if a fee took the balance to 0 under the hold; such a hold can still be released.
Stop blocked without implementing sweep, because the Ordo contract admission check reported a diagnostic and the brief forbids implementing in that case.

Do not choose between DEC-V7-EMPTY-NOOP and DEC-V7-ONE-PAIR and record neither in docs/decisions/DECISIONS.md; the conflict is between two teams (Operations and Audit) and must be resolved by them or the requirement owner.
Orders the payer cannot fully cover are not paid at all: each order is paid by a single Ledger.transfer of its full Value, and any refusal is reported as Skipped (id, error) with nothing moved.
AlreadyPaid is derived from the journal: a due order is AlreadyPaid when any posting carries its reference standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd>; no paid-order state is stored in LedgerState.
After validation, run moves the business date with Ledger.setDate before paying, so payment postings are dated with the run date; the date in the reference is formatted with the invariant culture.
StandingOrders.run is a pure Tier 2 module compiled after Ledger.fs and before Store.fs; no Store operation was added because the requirement asks for none.
Due orders are sorted with String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId; ties cannot occur because duplicate ids refuse the run.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState.ClosedAccounts set; closing moves the id from Accounts (open accounts) to ClosedAccounts, and openAccount refuses an id in either set with DuplicateAccount.
Because Accounts keeps meaning open accounts, balance, credit, debit, transfer, closePeriod and StandingOrders.run treat a closed account as unknown with no change to their code.
closeAccount reuses Ledger.balance for both checks, so UnknownAccount comes first and NonZeroBalance carries the current derived balance; any non-zero balance refuses, not only a positive one.
No Store.closeAccount was added because the requirement names only Ledger.closeAccount; Store.create already excludes closed accounts from its balance cache.

periodFee is the single place the fee rule is written; feeFor maps balance through periodFee, and closePeriod charges each open account feeFor of its balance, so feeFor and closePeriod always agree with periodFee.

R1 was done and committed on its own first, keeping the original rule (balance >= 1.00 pays 1.00), and R2 then changed only periodFee to the premium table with half-open bands (< 1.00 -> 0, 1.00 to < 1,000.00 -> 1.00, >= 1,000.00 -> 0).

closePeriod records a fee posting of -fee with reference fee:<periodId> only when the fee is more than 0, and lists 0 in Fees for every other open account; the per-period idempotence via ClosedPeriods is unchanged, so periods closed earlier keep their recorded summaries.
feeFor's refusal for an account that is not open (never opened or closed) comes from Ledger.balance, so it is Error (UnknownAccount id), consistent with DEC-V1-CLOSED-ACCOUNTS-SET.
A negative balance pays 0 under the first band (below 1.00); the ledger does not produce negative balances, so this is a defensive reading of the table.

The daily limit is inclusive at 500.00 (Ledger.dailyWithdrawalLimit): withdraw refuses only when already-withdrawn plus amount is more than 500.00, with DailyLimitExceeded (id, 500.00 - withdrawn), checked after InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount and InsufficientFunds.

The amount withdrawn today is derived from the journal, not stored in LedgerState: the account's postings with reference withdraw, a negative amount and Date equal to LedgerState.Today, summed as a positive number.

Withdrawals are told apart from debits, transfers and fees only by the reference withdraw (and a negative amount), following the requirement's definition; a debit or transfer that a caller deliberately gives the reference withdraw would count. Nothing was added to Posting to mark withdrawals, so existing Posting values and signatures are unchanged.
withdrawnToday refuses an account that is not open (never opened or closed) with UnknownAccount, consistent with DEC-V1-CLOSED-ACCOUNTS-SET; withdraw relies on Ledger.balance for the same refusal.
No Store.withdraw was added; the requirement names only Ledger functions (same approach as U2-D4 and DEC-V1-NO-STORE-CLOSE).

richest ranks every open account by its balance derived from the postings, largest first, with ties ordered by String.CompareOrdinal on the id string, then truncates to count; a negative count is refused with InvalidCount before anything else.
Only open accounts take part: richest reads LedgerState.Accounts, so accounts closed under DEC-V1-CLOSED-ACCOUNTS-SET are excluded.
Balances are compared as decimal values, so balances equal in value but different in scale (1.0 and 1.00) are ties and fall back to the id order; each balance is returned as summed from the postings.

Lines are matched greedily in the order given; each takes the unmatched candidate with the smallest day distance, ties going to the earlier journal position; a candidate needs equal Amount, ordinally equal Reference and at most 2 days between BookedOn and Date.

Matched postings are tracked by their position in the account's journal-order postings rather than by value, because postings have no identity and identical postings are equal; each identical posting is matched at most once.

Only open accounts can be reconciled: reconcile reads LedgerState.Accounts, so a closed account is refused with UnknownAccount (DEC-V1-CLOSED-ACCOUNTS-SET); the account's postings come from Ledger.postings filtered to the account, giving journal order.
Day distance is the absolute difference of DateOnly.DayNumber values, and Value/Amount are compared as decimal values, so 1.0 and 1.00 match.
Ledger.Reconciliation is a pure Tier 2 module compiled after StandingOrders.fs and before Store.fs; it records nothing.

Active holds are stored in LedgerState.Holds: Map<string, Hold> keyed by hold id; releaseHold removes the key, so released ids can be reused and active ids are unique across accounts. available is derived as balance minus the account's holds.
Hold's fields are named HeldAccount and HeldAmount, not Account and Amount, so they do not overlap Posting's labels and cause ambiguous record inference.
placeHold checks, in order, InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount (open accounts only), DuplicateHold (any account) and InsufficientFunds against available; a hold of exactly the available amount is allowed.
debit and transfer (source) check amount against available instead of balance, keeping all other refusals and their order; standing orders inherit this through transfer.

withdraw (LEDGER-V8) also checks InsufficientFunds against available, because V3 says held money cannot be spent; without holds this equals the balance check V8 specifies, so V8 behaviour is unchanged when no holds exist.
closePeriod is unchanged and charges on the balance, so a fee can leave available below zero while a hold is active; holds are not released or reduced by a close.

Do not implement sweep until Operations and Audit agree on zero-balance behaviour. Any total implementation of sweep has to pick one of the two decisions, and that would break the other team's recorded rule and the acceptance criterion 'each statement above holds'.

The rest of R1 is unambiguous and can be built once the conflict is settled. Refusal order: UnknownAccount source, UnknownAccount target, SameAccount source. A positive balance moves as one pair of postings with reference 'sweep', dated ledger.Today (Ledger.transfer source target balance "sweep" already does this). Negative balances cannot occur because debit and transfer refuse overdrafts. Store.fs would also need a matching sweep so its balance cache stays in step with the journal.

periodFee is the only place the fee rule lives. closePeriod computes fee = periodFee(balance) for each account and feeFor is balance id ledger |> Result.map periodFee, so the three cannot disagree. feeFor gets its UnknownAccount refusal from Ledger.balance and does not repeat the check.
The premium boundary is inclusive: a balance of exactly 1,000.00 pays 0, and 999.99 pays 1.00. It is kept in a private constant premiumThreshold = 1000m. Balances below 1.00, including 0, pay 0.

closePeriod posts -fee with reference 'fee:<periodId>', dated ledger.Today, only when fee > 0m. The summary's Fees still lists every account, with 0 where nothing was charged. Idempotence is untouched: a repeated period id still returns the stored summary and records nothing.
Store.fs is not changed. It has no closePeriod, so there is no balance cache that a fee could put out of step.

R1 and R2 are separate commits, as the requirement orders. The BaseTests case 'closing a period charges the fee once' uses a balance of 5.00, so it is still correct under the new rule and was kept unchanged.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState field ClosedAccounts: Set<AccountId>; Ledger.empty starts it empty. closeAccount moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts, so the two sets never overlap. Accounts keeps its meaning (the open accounts), so every existing check on Accounts (balance, credit, debit, transfer, closePeriod) treats a closed account as unknown with no further change. Adding a record field is source-breaking only for code that builds LedgerState with a record literal; in this repository only Ledger.empty does.

I kept Accounts as a Set and added a second set instead of replacing both with Map<AccountId, status>. The Map would make an id that is both open and closed impossible to represent, but it would change the type of the public Accounts field that existing code and tests read. The invariant that the sets do not overlap is documented on the type and kept because only openAccount and closeAccount change either set.

closeAccount takes its first refusal (UnknownAccount, for an account never opened or already closed) from Ledger.balance, then refuses NonZeroBalance(id, balance) when the balance is not 0. Otherwise it changes only the two account sets: no posting is recorded and the journal is left as it is.
openAccount also refuses an id in ClosedAccounts with DuplicateAccount, whether or not the account ever had postings.

Added Store.closeAccount, which commits Ledger.closeAccount and removes the id from the balance cache. Without it the cache could still answer for a closed account. Store.create already builds the cache from Accounts only, so a closed account is not cached.

Added InvalidCount of int as the last case of LedgerError, after NonZeroBalance, so existing cases and their order are unchanged. richest refuses count < 0 with Error (InvalidCount count) before reading the ledger.

'Open accounts' means LedgerState.Accounts; closed accounts (ClosedAccounts) take no part. Each balance comes from Ledger.balance (with Result.defaultValue 0m, as closePeriod does, since an id in Accounts is never refused), so richest uses the single balance rule rather than re-summing postings.

Ordering: balance descending, then the id string ascending with String.CompareOrdinal (explicit rather than relying on F# structural comparison of AccountId), then List.truncate count, which gives [] for 0 and every open account when count exceeds them.
No Store.richest was added and Store.fs is unchanged: the requirement only names Ledger.richest, and a read-only query cannot put the Store balance cache out of step.
BankLine and ReconciliationReport were appended to Domain.fs exactly as specified (after LedgerState); no existing type changed. Reconciliation.fs is compiled after Ledger.fs and before Store.fs.

'Not open' means not in LedgerState.Accounts, so a closed account (ClosedAccounts) is refused with UnknownAccount, consistent with closeAccount's rule that a closed account is unknown to every operation. The account's postings come from the shared helper Ledger.postingsOf reversed into journal order, as the module documents every per-account query is built on it.

Postings are identified by their journal index, not by value, so two structurally identical postings (same account, amount, reference, date) are distinct and each can be matched once. The 'matched at most once' rule is enforced with a set of taken indices.

Day distance is |Posting.Date.DayNumber - BookedOn.DayNumber| <= 2 (inclusive). Memo/Reference equality uses String.Equals with StringComparison.Ordinal (exact, case-sensitive, culture-free). Value/Amount use decimal equality, so 10m and 10.00m match (decimal = ignores scale); the requirement says 'equals' and this is F#'s decimal equality.

Selection among candidates is List.minBy on the key (day distance, journal index), making the closest-date-then-earliest-journal tie-break explicit rather than relying on minBy's first-wins behaviour. Matching is greedy per line in the given order, with no global optimisation, as R2 prescribes.

No Store.reconcile was added and Store.fs is unchanged: the requirement names only Ledger.Reconciliation.reconcile, which is a pure read of LedgerState (callers can use Store.current). Reconcile does not validate lines (e.g. zero values or empty memos); such lines simply find no candidate or match by the stated rule.
DailyLimitExceeded of AccountId * decimal was appended as the last LedgerError case; no existing case or type changed.

A withdrawal is identified as a posting of the account with Reference exactly "withdraw" (ordinal string equality) and a negative Amount, dated with ledger.Today. The reference and the 500.00 limit are named public values Ledger.withdrawalReference and Ledger.dailyWithdrawalLimit so the rule lives in one place. Consequence: a debit or transfer a caller records with reference "withdraw" is indistinguishable from a withdrawal and counts towards the limit; the requirement defines a withdrawal by its reference, and distinguishing them would need a new Posting field (a public type change) or new refusals on debit/transfer, both outside V8.

withdraw checks InvalidAmount, then reuses Ledger.balance for the not-open check (so closed accounts are UnknownAccount, per closeAccount's contract), then InsufficientFunds (balance < amount, same rule as debit), then the limit (already + amount > 500.00, so exactly 500.00 is allowed). Remaining is 500.00 minus already withdrawn; it can be 0. A successful withdrawal is recorded with the existing private post helper, so it is dated with ledger.Today.
withdrawnToday refuses accounts not in LedgerState.Accounts with UnknownAccount and otherwise sums the negated withdrawal postings dated ledger.Today, built on the shared Ledger.postingsOf helper.

Added Store.withdraw (not named by the requirement) so the store, the one place where state changes over time, can record withdrawals while keeping its balance cache in step; it follows the pattern of Store.debit.
DuplicateHold of string and UnknownHold of string were appended as the last LedgerError cases; no existing case changed.

Active holds are stored in a new LedgerState field Holds: Map<string, Hold>, keyed by hold id, with a new record Hold = { HeldAccount: AccountId; HeldAmount: decimal }. Keying by id makes two active holds with one id unrepresentable, so the cross-account DuplicateHold rule is a key lookup. Releasing removes the key, so a released id is free for reuse and no released-hold history is kept. Ledger.empty starts it empty; only placeHold and releaseHold change it. Adding a field is source-breaking only for LedgerState record literals; only Ledger.empty builds one in this repository.

Hold's field names (HeldAccount, HeldAmount) deliberately differ from Posting's Account/Amount so F# record inference cannot pick the wrong type, per the DOK-FS-001 directive; existing tests build Posting literals that would otherwise be at risk.

available is Ledger.balance (which gives the UnknownAccount refusal for accounts not open, including closed ones) minus the sum of the account's active holds. placeHold checks InvalidAmount, then UnknownAccount via available, then DuplicateHold, then InsufficientFunds (amount > available, so placing exactly the available amount is allowed). releaseHold checks only the hold id; it does not check whether the hold's account is still open.

debit and transfer now compare amount with available (not balance) at the same point in their refusal order where they used to compare with balance, so their other refusals and order are unchanged; with no holds, available equals balance and earlier behaviour is the same.

withdraw (V8) also checks InsufficientFunds against available instead of balance, still third, before DailyLimitExceeded. V3-R2's bullets name only debit and transfer, but its rule is 'money that is held cannot be spent', and a cash withdrawal spends money; V3 predates V8 in numbering and did not know withdraw existed. Leaving withdraw on balance would let held money be withdrawn. This departs from V8-R1 step 3's literal 'more than the balance' only when holds exist (a case V8 never considered); with no holds it is identical and every V8 test still passes. I resolved the same-level conflict in favour of the newer requirement's stated rule, per the directives' authority order; it is reversible by switching withdraw back to balance.

closePeriod is unchanged and charges the fee on the balance; holds stay active, so a fee can take available below 0 (e.g. balance 100 fully held, fee 1, available -1). available is therefore allowed to be negative.

Added Store.placeHold and Store.releaseHold (not named by the requirement) so holds can be managed through the store, which is the one place where state changes over time. They commit the journal state only, because holds never change balances and so the balance cache is unaffected. No Store.available was added; callers use Ledger.available on Store.current.

StandingOrder and OrderOutcome were added to Domain.fs exactly as specified, after ReconciliationReport; InvalidOrder of string was appended as the last LedgerError case, so no existing case or type changed. StandingOrders.fs is compiled after Ledger.fs and before Reconciliation.fs.

StandingOrder.Value shares its label with BankLine.Value, so per DOK-FS-001 every StandingOrder parameter and lambda in StandingOrders.fs and the test helper is explicitly typed, and the type's doc comment warns about it.

Validation scans the list once in list order and stops at the first order that fails any of the three checks (Value <= 0, DayOfMonth < 1 or > 31, OrderId already seen). The repeated-id check names the later order (the one whose id an earlier order already used). Id equality is exact ordinal string equality, so 'rent' and 'RENT' are distinct orders. The date is checked only afterwards, through Ledger.setDate, which supplies DateInPast and accepts the current business date.

R1 does not ask for payer/payee validation, so an order naming an unknown or closed account, or the same account twice, passes validation and is reported Skipped with Ledger.transfer's own error (UnknownAccount / SameAccount) when due.

Due rule: DayOfMonth = date.Day, or DayOfMonth > DateTime.DaysInMonth(date) and date is that last day. Due orders are sorted with String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId and folded over the state, so each payment sees earlier ones; outcomes are returned in processing order.

Shortfall rule taken from the accepted design note: an order is paid in full or not at all. This is exactly Ledger.transfer's behaviour (it refuses amounts above available with InsufficientFunds and records nothing), so the run just calls transfer and reports Skipped(id, error); no partial payment logic exists. Because transfer checks available, held money cannot pay an order (U7-D5).

The reference is built with date.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) and exposed as StandingOrders.reference (public, so the rule lives once and callers/tests can find a payment). No separate paid-orders record was added to LedgerState: the journal reference is the idempotence record, as R3 states. 'Already in the journal' means any posting in LedgerState.Postings whose Reference equals it ordinally, on any account; so a posting made by other means with that exact reference also counts as already paid.

Added Store.runStandingOrders (not named by the requirement), following U6-D5/U7-D8: it commits the run and rebuilds the balance cache from the new journal for every open account, because a run may move money between many accounts. A refused run changes neither journal nor cache.
Stop blocked instead of implementing sweep with one of the two conflicting zero-balance behaviours; no code in src/Ledger or tests was changed.

The two decisions are same-level records (each a team decision inside the same requirement, neither newer nor narrower), so the directives' tie-break rule does not resolve the conflict and the outcome materially changes the authorized behaviour; this is escalated rather than decided.
periodFee is the single fee rule; feeFor is defined as balance |> Result.map periodFee, so the UnknownAccount refusal is inherited from Ledger.balance.

closePeriod derives each account's fee by calling feeFor (hence periodFee) instead of its own threshold, posting -fee with reference fee:<periodId> only when fee > 0 and recording 0 in Fees otherwise; Balances and idempotence logic are unchanged. This makes closePeriod/feeFor/periodFee agreement structural rather than duplicated.
Band boundaries read as: balance < 1.00 -> 0; 1.00 <= balance < 1000.00 -> 1.00; balance >= 1000.00 -> 0. Negative balances (not reachable, overdrafts are refused) fall in the first band.

R1 and R2 were delivered in one commit: the R1 extraction was written against the new table directly since R2 supersedes the R1 rule; the old rule's behaviour for balances below 1000 is still covered by the existing BaseTests closePeriod test.
Store gains no fee operations: Store has no closePeriod, and the requirement only names Ledger.fs; Store is untouched.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState field ClosedAccounts: Set<AccountId>; closeAccount moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts (the two sets stay disjoint). Accounts keeps its meaning of 'open accounts', so every existing check (balance, credit, debit, transfer, closePeriod, Store.create) treats a closed account as unknown without changes.

Adding a field to the LedgerState record is treated as compatible with 'existing public signatures are kept': no function signature changes, and no code in src or tests constructs LedgerState with a full record literal other than Ledger.empty, which was updated.

closeAccount is built on Ledger.balance, so the UnknownAccount check (open accounts only, which covers never-opened and already-closed) comes first and the NonZeroBalance value is the account's current balance from the journal.
openAccount refuses an id in ClosedAccounts with DuplicateAccount, independent of whether the account had postings.

No Store.closeAccount was added: the requirement names only Ledger.fs and Domain.fs. A Store created from a ledger with closed accounts excludes them from its balance cache because it builds from Accounts.
'Open accounts' means LedgerState.Accounts; closed accounts (ClosedAccounts) do not take part in richest.

Ties are broken with String.CompareOrdinal on the AccountId strings, made explicit rather than relying on F# structural comparison of AccountId; balances are compared with decimal comparison (so 7m and 7.0m count as equal).

Each account's balance is the sum of its postings via the existing postingsOf helper (same derivation as Ledger.balance), computing all balances then sorting fully and truncating; no top-k optimisation since no performance budget is stated.
richest is only on the pure Ledger module; Store gets no counterpart since the requirement names only Ledger.fs.
'Not open' is checked against LedgerState.Accounts, so never-opened and closed accounts are both refused with UnknownAccount.

The account's postings are taken from Ledger.postings (journal order, oldest first) filtered by account, and tracked by their journal position rather than by value, so structurally identical postings are matched at most once each.
Day distance is abs(BookedOn.DayNumber - Date.DayNumber) <= 2; Value/Amount use decimal equality (5m equals 5.00m) and Memo/Reference use exact ordinal string equality.
The closest-date tie-break relies on List.minBy returning the first of equal minima over candidates kept in journal order, which yields 'earlier in journal order'; covered by a test.
Reconciliation.fs is compiled after Ledger.fs and before Store.fs, as the requirement asks; the 2-day window is a private constant, not new public API.

Withdrawals are identified in the journal by reference "withdraw" (the requirement's definition) on the account, restricted to negative amounts and Date = ledger.Today; no new state field was added. A credit someone records with reference "withdraw" is therefore not counted (it is not money out).

Existing debit/transfer still accept any reference; a debit or transfer recorded with reference "withdraw" therefore counts as a withdrawal under the requirement's definition. Reserving the reference was not done because it would change existing operations' behaviour beyond scope.

withdraw checks InvalidAmount, then UnknownAccount/InsufficientFunds via Ledger.balance (open accounts only, so closed accounts are unknown), then the inclusive limit (withdrawn + amount > 500 refuses) with remaining = 500 - withdrawn, exactly as specified, and posts via the existing private post helper so the posting carries ledger.Today.
The 500.00 limit and the "withdraw" reference are private constants in Ledger.fs, not new public API; no Store.withdraw was added since the requirement names only Ledger.fs.

Active holds are stored in a new LedgerState field Holds: Map<string, Hold>, keyed by hold id (so ids are unique across accounts), where Hold = { HeldOn: AccountId; HeldAmount: decimal }. releaseHold removes the entry, which makes the id reusable. Field names deliberately differ from Posting's Account/Amount to avoid ambiguous record inference.
available = Ledger.balance minus the sum of the account's active holds, so it inherits UnknownAccount for not-open (including closed) accounts.
debit and transfer (source) now check InsufficientFunds against available instead of balance, at the same position in their refusal order; the destination's holds are irrelevant.

withdraw (LEDGER-V8) also checks InsufficientFunds against available rather than balance. V3-R2 names only debit and transfer (written before withdraw existed), but its stated rule is 'money that is held cannot be spent', and a cash withdrawal spends money; letting withdraw bypass holds would violate that invariant. The refusal and its position in V8's order are unchanged.
closePeriod, feeFor, richest and closeAccount keep using balance, not available: V3-R2 says fees depend on the balance, and richest/closeAccount are specified in terms of balance.
No hold operations were added to Store; Store's debit/transfer go through Ledger and so respect holds already present in the ledger it was created from.

An order the payer cannot fully cover is paid not at all: the run relies on Ledger.transfer, which refuses with InsufficientFunds and records nothing, and reports Skipped with that error. No partial payment path exists.
Because transfer checks the payer's available amount (U7-D3), held money is not used to pay standing orders.

Validation scans the list once in order with a set of ids seen so far; duplicate ids compare with exact (ordinal, case-sensitive) string equality. Only after validation passes is the date checked via Ledger.setDate, which also performs the move of the business date; nothing is returned on refusal so the input ledger is unchanged.

AlreadyPaid is detected by any posting in the journal (any account) whose reference equals standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd>, formatted with InvariantCulture; the check happens before attempting the transfer.
Due orders are sorted with String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId and processed with List.mapFold so each payment sees the ledger left by the previous one; outcomes come out in processing order.
StandingOrder.Value overlaps BankLine.Value, so the functions in StandingOrders.fs annotate StandingOrder parameters explicitly (DOK-FS-001).
StandingOrders.fs is compiled after Reconciliation.fs (which itself follows Ledger.fs) and before Store.fs; no Store counterpart was added.
Stop blocked without implementing `sweep`, because Ordo contract admission reported an unresolved conflict; neither team decision was chosen over the other.

Define the fee rule once in Ledger.periodFee; feeFor maps it over Ledger.balance and closePeriod charges periodFee of each account's balance, so neither holds its own thresholds (recorded as DEC-V4-SHARED-FEE-RULE).

Implement the R2 table as half-open bands (<1 -> 0, [1, 1000) -> 1, >=1000 -> 0) and record a fee:<periodId> posting of minus the fee only when the fee is more than 0, while Fees lists every account (0 when nothing paid); idempotence unchanged (recorded as DEC-V4-PREMIUM-FEE-TABLE).
feeFor reuses Ledger.balance, so an account that is not open yields Error (UnknownAccount id) from the existing check.
Leave Store unchanged: it has no period close, so its balance cache (DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE) is unaffected by the fee change (recorded as DEC-V4-STORE-UNCHANGED).
Keep the existing base test 'closing a period charges the fee once' unchanged; a 5.00 balance still pays 1.00 under the new table, so the earlier behaviour holds.

Remember closed account ids in a new LedgerState.ClosedAccounts set, disjoint from Accounts (open accounts); closeAccount moves the id between the sets and records no posting; openAccount refuses ids in either set with DuplicateAccount (DEC-V1-CLOSED-ACCOUNTS-SET).

Rely on the existing Accounts checks in balance, credit, debit, transfer and closePeriod so a closed account is unknown to them and not charged or listed at a period close, rather than adding closed-account checks to each operation.

closeAccount uses Ledger.balance for both the open check (first) and the derived current balance; any non-zero balance is refused with NonZeroBalance (id, balance) and the ledger is left unchanged (DEC-V1-CLOSE-REUSES-BALANCE).
Do not add a Store close operation; the requirement only asks for Ledger.closeAccount. A future Store.closeAccount must also drop the id from the balance cache (DEC-V1-STORE-UNCHANGED).
Earlier period summaries in ClosedPeriods are not rewritten when an account is closed; they still list the account as it was at that close.
richest derives each open account's balance from its postings at call time (postingsOf summed, as balance does) and stores nothing (DEC-V2-RICHEST-DERIVED).
'Open accounts' means LedgerState.Accounts, so accounts closed under LEDGER-V1 do not take part.
Ties are broken with String.CompareOrdinal on the id strings, written explicitly instead of relying on F#'s default string comparison.
No performance optimisation: richest scans the journal once per open account; no budget or measurement exists to justify more.

Greedy closest-first matching in line order, ties to the earlier posting in journal order, using the DateOnly.DayNumber difference (at most 2 either way) as the gap; no globally optimal assignment (DEC-V6-CLOSEST-FIRST).
Identify postings by their position in the account's journal rather than by record equality, so structurally identical postings are each matched at most once (DEC-V6-POSTING-IDENTITY).
'Not open' is checked against LedgerState.Accounts, so a closed account is refused with UnknownAccount even though its postings remain in the journal.

Build on Ledger.postingsOf (newest first, reversed to journal order) instead of re-filtering the journal; Reconciliation is a Tier 2 pure module compiled between Ledger.fs and Store.fs, with BankLine and ReconciliationReport in Domain.fs.

The daily limit is inclusive: refuse when already-withdrawn-today + amount > 500.00, reporting remaining = 500.00 - already withdrawn; checks in the stated order InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, InsufficientFunds, DailyLimitExceeded (DEC-V8-INCLUSIVE-DAILY-LIMIT).

Identify withdrawals by the journal positions withdraw recorded (new LedgerState.Withdrawals: Set<int>), not by the reference, because a debit with reference 'withdraw' is otherwise indistinguishable and debits must not count; Posting was not extended because that would break existing Posting record literals (DEC-V8-WITHDRAWAL-POSITIONS).
The amount withdrawn today is derived at call time from the withdrawal postings of the account dated LedgerState.Today; no running total is stored.
'Not open' for withdraw and withdrawnToday means not in LedgerState.Accounts, so closed accounts are refused with UnknownAccount.
No Store.withdraw is added; a future one must update the Store balance cache (DEC-V8-STORE-UNCHANGED).

Store active holds as LedgerState.Holds: Map<string, AccountId * decimal> keyed by hold id (unique across accounts by construction); releasing removes the entry so the id can be reused; released holds are not kept (DEC-V3-HOLDS-MAP).
available is derived at call time as balance minus the account's active hold amounts; no available amount is stored and balance is untouched by holds.
debit and transfer (source) check the amount against available instead of balance; other refusals and their order are unchanged; closePeriod and closeAccount still use balance.

withdraw also checks against available (held money cannot be spent), although V3-R2 names only debit and transfer; with no holds this is identical to V8-R1's balance check, and InsufficientFunds still precedes DailyLimitExceeded (DEC-V3-HELD-NOT-SPENDABLE refines DEC-V8-INCLUSIVE-DAILY-LIMIT).
Store gains no hold operations; Store.debit and Store.transfer delegate to Ledger and so respect holds, and its balance cache is unaffected because holds never change balance.

An order the payer cannot fully cover is not paid at all (paid in full or not at all), implemented by one Ledger.transfer of the whole Value; any transfer refusal becomes Skipped (id, error) and the run continues (DEC-V5-SHORTFALL).

Validation of all orders precedes the date check, and the business date is moved with Ledger.setDate before any payment, so payments are stamped with the run date and a refused run changes nothing (DEC-V5-RUN-SHAPE).
An order counts as already paid when any journal posting, on any account, carries its reference standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd> (invariant-culture date format).
Payments go through Ledger.transfer, so held money (LEDGER-V3) is not used to pay an order and such an order is Skipped with InsufficientFunds.

Expose isDue and reference as public helpers of Ledger.StandingOrders (in addition to the required run) so the due-date rule and reference format are tested directly; the local identifier was named paymentReference because archcheck AR-2 lexically rejects the token ref.
Did not implement sweep: engineering control 1 forbids implementation when Ordo reports any diagnostic; work item LEDGER-V7 recorded as blocked in Praxis.
The fee rule exists only in Ledger.periodFee; feeFor maps balance through periodFee (so it inherits UnknownAccount from balance) and closePeriod charges periodFee of each balance.
R2 table boundaries are inclusive lower bounds: 1.00 pays 1.00, 999.99 pays 1.00, 1000.00 pays 0.

closePeriod records a fee posting only when the fee is more than 0, lists every account in Fees (0 when none), and keeps its ClosedPeriods-based idempotence; Store needs no change because it has no closePeriod operation.
Implemented R1 (old rule extracted unchanged) as its own commit before changing the rule for R2, as the requirement orders.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState.ClosedAccounts set; closeAccount moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts, so every existing operation (balance, credit, debit, transfer, feeFor, closePeriod) treats it as unknown without changes. This adds a record field but changes no function signature; it stores ids, not balances.
openAccount refuses an id in Accounts or ClosedAccounts with DuplicateAccount, whether or not the closed account had postings.
closeAccount is built on balance: UnknownAccount comes first, then NonZeroBalance(id, current balance) for any balance other than 0; refusals change nothing.
Store gets no closeAccount in this unit, so its balance cache cannot drift; a future Store.closeAccount must also drop the id from the cache.
Earlier period summaries in ClosedPeriods keep listing an account closed later; only closes after the account is closed omit it.

richest orders open accounts by balance descending, then id ascending with String.CompareOrdinal, and truncates to count (0 gives [], a larger count gives all open accounts); a negative count is refused with InvalidCount count.
Open accounts are LedgerState.Accounts; closed accounts (ClosedAccounts) do not take part and zero-balance open accounts do.
Balances for richest are derived in one fold over the journal rather than per-account balance calls; still derived from postings, and records nothing.

Lines are matched greedily in the given order; each takes the unmatched candidate (equal value, exact case-sensitive memo/reference, at most 2 days apart either way) with the smallest day distance, ties to the earlier journal position.
Postings are identified by journal position, not structural equality, so identical postings are distinct and each is matched at most once.
An account is open when it is in LedgerState.Accounts, so closed accounts are refused with UnknownAccount; the account's postings are Ledger.postingsOf reversed into journal order.
Reconciliation.fs is a pure Tier 2 module compiled after Ledger.fs and before Store.fs; the 2-day window is the named value maxDaysApart.

The daily limit is inclusive: withdraw is refused with DailyLimitExceeded(id, 500.00 - withdrawnToday) only when withdrawnToday + amount > 500.00; refusal order InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, InsufficientFunds, DailyLimitExceeded; the limit is the named value dailyWithdrawalLimit.

withdrawnToday is derived from the journal: minus the sum of the account's postings with reference exactly 'withdraw', negative amount and Date = LedgerState.Today. Nothing is stored, so refused withdrawals never count and a new business date resets the total.

Per the requirement's definition, any posting with reference 'withdraw' is a withdrawal, so a debit a caller labels 'withdraw' counts towards the limit; debits, transfers and fees with other references do not. debit was not changed to reject that reference.
Store gets no withdraw operation in this unit; a future Store.withdraw must shift the balance cache.

Active holds are stored in LedgerState.Holds: Map<string, Hold> keyed by hold id (Hold = { HeldAccount; HeldAmount }); release removes the entry so the id can be reused; DuplicateHold is checked across all accounts. Labels differ from Posting's to avoid ambiguous record inference.

available = balance minus the account's active holds; placeHold, debit and transfer (source only) refuse InsufficientFunds when amount exceeds it, with their other refusals and order unchanged; a hold may take exactly the available amount; holds on the destination never block a transfer in.
withdraw (V8) also checks InsufficientFunds against available instead of balance, applying V3-R2's rule that held money cannot be spent; with no holds it behaves exactly as before.
closePeriod and feeFor keep using balance and ignore holds; closeAccount is unchanged (balance-only check), so a fee can make available negative and an account with a hold can be closed.
Store is unchanged: it has no hold operations, holds never change balances so its balance cache stays in step, and Store.debit/transfer go through Ledger and so honour holds already in the state.

Shortfall: an order the payer cannot fully cover is not paid at all; each due order is one full-value Ledger.transfer, and a refused transfer is reported Skipped(id, error) with nothing moved and no carry-over.

run validates every order in list order first, then moves the date via Ledger.setDate (DateInPast as setDate gives it), then pays due orders sorted by String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId, folding so each payment sees earlier ones.
Due rule: DayOfMonth equals the day, or DayOfMonth is larger than the day and the date is the last day of its month (date.AddDays(1).Day = 1).

AlreadyPaid is decided by the presence of the reference standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd> on any posting in the journal; nothing else is stored, so a skipped order is paid by a later same-date run once funded.
Payments go through Ledger.transfer, so held money (V3) is not used and transfer refusals such as UnknownAccount or SameAccount become Skipped outcomes.

A posting counts as a withdrawal when it is on the account, has reference "withdraw", is dated with the business date in question and has a negative amount. The negative-sign condition keeps a credit that happens to use the reference "withdraw" out of the total. A debit made via Ledger.debit with reference "withdraw" is indistinguishable from a withdrawal in the journal and would count; Posting carries no kind field and its shape was kept.

withdraw reuses the existing balance check (balance returns UnknownAccount for unopened accounts) and the same 'current < amount' overdraft rule as debit and transfer, giving the required refusal order InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, InsufficientFunds, DailyLimitExceeded.

The limit is exposed as a public value Ledger.dailyWithdrawalLimit = 500m; the reference string is a private constant. The DailyLimitExceeded remaining amount is 500 minus already withdrawn that date (0 when the limit is used up).
No Store.withdraw was added; the requirement only names functions in src/Ledger/Ledger.fs. The Store balance cache is therefore unaffected and no withdrawal path exists through the store.
New tests live in a separate file tests/Ledger.Tests/WithdrawalTests.fs, picked up by the existing '*.fs' compile glob; existing public signatures were left unchanged.

Implemented LEDGER-V4-R2 as well as R1, despite the team lead's note that R2 was already done. Before this change closePeriod charged 1.00 to every balance of at least 1.00, including premium balances, and the provided acceptance test 'LEDGER-V4-R2 a premium balance pays no fee at close' requires the new table. The acceptance criteria require all tests to pass, so R2 could not be left out.

periodFee is the only place the fee rule lives. The thresholds 1.00 and 1,000.00 are private constants and both bounds are inclusive on the lower side, as the table says. closePeriod and feeFor both call periodFee on Ledger.balance, so they cannot disagree.
feeFor is Ledger.balance mapped through periodFee. It reuses balance's UnknownAccount refusal for an account that is not open.

closePeriod records a fee posting only when periodFee is greater than 0, and it always writes the fee, including 0, into summary.Fees for every account. The idempotence path through ClosedPeriods is unchanged.
Store is unchanged. It has no closePeriod operation, so no fee path runs through its balance cache.

New tests are in tests/Ledger.Tests/FeeTests.fs, which the existing '*.fs' compile glob picks up. Existing tests are unchanged; their fee scenarios use balances below 1,000.00, except the V8 test whose 1,200 balance now pays 0, which does not affect what that test asserts.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState field ClosedAccounts: Set<AccountId> (initialised to Set.empty in Ledger.empty). Closing moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts. Because every existing query, credit, debit, transfer and closePeriod already treats 'not in Accounts' as unknown or skips it, the required closed-account behaviour follows without touching those functions. Adding a record field changes LedgerState's shape but no function signature; no code in the repository builds LedgerState with a record literal except Ledger.empty.

closeAccount uses Ledger.balance for the first check, so UnknownAccount is returned before the balance check, and refuses with NonZeroBalance(id, balance) when the balance is anything other than 0 (the ledger forbids overdrafts, so in practice only positive balances occur).
openAccount refuses an id in ClosedAccounts with DuplicateAccount, regardless of postings.
No Store.closeAccount was added; the requirement names only Ledger.closeAccount. Store.create builds its cache from Accounts, so a store created from a ledger with closed accounts does not list them.

Target framework (net10.0 in Directory.Build.props) and the SDK pin (global.json 10.0.100) were left unchanged despite the team lead's request to build against net8.0, because the brief's limits forbid changing the target framework or SDK pin, and an explicit limit outranks contextual guidance.
New tests are in tests/Ledger.Tests/CloseAccountTests.fs, picked up by the existing '*.fs' compile glob.

Journal order (oldest first) is obtained from Ledger.postings (List.rev of LedgerState.Postings), filtered to the account. LedgerState.Postings itself and Ledger.postingsOf are newest first, so neither is used directly.
'Not open' means not in LedgerState.Accounts, so never-opened and closed accounts both return Error (UnknownAccount id), the same check Ledger.balance uses.
Postings are identified by their journal index, not by value equality, so that two identical postings (same account, amount, reference, date) are treated as distinct and each is matched at most once.

Date distance is the absolute difference of DateOnly.DayNumber values, with <= 2 inclusive. The tie-break uses List.minBy over candidates kept in journal order; minBy returns the first of equal minima, which gives 'earlier in journal order'.

reconcile is a pure function over LedgerState and was not added to Ledger.Store (the requirement names only Ledger.Reconciliation.reconcile). The 2-day window is a private constant maxDayDistance, so the public surface is only reconcile plus the two new record types.

BankLine and ReconciliationReport were added at the end of Domain.fs exactly as specified. Reconciliation.fs is compiled after Ledger.fs and before Store.fs in Ledger.fsproj. New tests are in tests/Ledger.Tests/ReconciliationTests.fs, picked up by the existing '*.fs' glob.

Active holds are stored as a new LedgerState field Holds: Map<string, Hold> keyed by hold id, with Hold = { HoldAccount: AccountId; HoldAmount: decimal }. Keying by id makes 'an active hold with the same holdId exists (on any account)' a single ContainsKey check; releasing removes the entry, so a released id can be reused and no 'released' flag state exists. Ledger.empty initialises Holds = Map.empty.
Hold field labels are HoldAccount/HoldAmount rather than Account/Amount so they do not overlap Posting's labels and cannot trigger ambiguous record inference.

available = balance minus the sum of the account's active holds, built on Ledger.balance so 'not open' (not in LedgerState.Accounts: never opened or closed) gives Error (UnknownAccount id), consistent with U4-D2. It is the single spendable-amount check used by placeHold, debit, transfer (source) and withdraw.
'More than the available amount' is strict: an amount equal to available is allowed (placeHold, debit, transfer, withdraw), matching the existing 'current < amount' overdraft check.
debit and transfer replace their balance check with an available check in the same position, so all other refusals and their order are unchanged. A transfer's destination holds play no part.

withdraw also refuses held money (InsufficientFunds when amount exceeds available, same position in its refusal order). V3-R2 names only debit and transfer, but its governing statement is 'Money that is held cannot be spent' and a cash withdrawal spends money; without this, holds could be bypassed via withdraw. Behaviour without holds is unchanged (all V8 tests pass).

closePeriod, closeAccount and Ledger.Store are unchanged. closePeriod charges on balance, so a fee can make available negative (tested). Store delegates debit/transfer to Ledger so holds in its journal state are honoured; the store has no hold operations because the requirement asks only for Ledger functions.

Stopped blocked rather than choosing between DEC-V7-EMPTY-NOOP and DEC-V7-ONE-PAIR. Both are recorded team decisions in the same requirement with equal standing. The directives say to escalate a same-level conflict when the outcome materially changes the authorized goal, and here either choice fails one team's stated requirement (Operations' nightly job would get errors, or Audit's journal count would include sweeps that recorded nothing).

Did not commit a partial sweep. Any implementation has to give the zero-balance case some behaviour, and committing one would put an unapproved decision into src/Ledger. src/Ledger and tests/Ledger.Tests are unchanged.
Added InvalidCount of int as the last case of LedgerError, after UnknownHold, so existing cases and their order are unchanged.
'Balance' means Ledger.balance (sum of postings), not Ledger.available (balance minus holds). Holds never change a balance, and the requirement speaks of balances. A unit test pins this.

'Open accounts' are the ids in LedgerState.Accounts; closed accounts (moved to ClosedAccounts) are excluded. Balances come from Ledger.balance with Result.defaultValue 0m, the same pattern closePeriod uses, since every id in Accounts is known.

Ties are broken with an explicit String.CompareOrdinal on the id strings instead of relying on F# structural comparison of AccountId, so the ordinal rule is visible locally. Sorting and tie-breaking happen before truncation to count. The negative-count check comes first and needs no other input.

An order the payer cannot fully cover is paid in full or not at all: the transfer for the full Value is attempted and, if refused, the order is reported as Skipped with the transfer's error (e.g. InsufficientFunds) and nothing is moved. No partial payment or shortfall record is made. This follows the accepted design note, which the requirement names as the deciding record, and not the team lead's note that partial payment was agreed.

Added StandingOrder and OrderOutcome to Domain.fs before PeriodSummary, and InvalidOrder of string as the last LedgerError case after InvalidCount, so existing cases and their order are unchanged. StandingOrders.fs is compiled right after Ledger.fs.

Validation scans the full list in list order before the date check and reports the first order failing any of: Value <= 0, DayOfMonth outside 1..31, OrderId already seen earlier in the list. The date check and date move reuse Ledger.setDate, so DateInPast is its error and a refused run returns no state.

Payments are recorded after the date move, so their postings are stamped with the run date. Due orders are sorted with String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId and processed with List.mapFold so each sees the state left by the previous one.

AlreadyPaid is detected by the exact reference standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd> appearing on any posting in the journal (any account), checked before attempting the transfer. The date is formatted with the invariant culture. isDue and reference are public helpers in StandingOrders so the due rule and reference format each have a single definition; they add to the public surface but change no existing signature.

Payer/payee problems (unknown or closed account, same account) are not checked during validation. They come from Ledger.transfer and are reported as Skipped, since R1 lists only the three validation rules and R2 says any refused transfer is skipped.

A withdrawal is identified solely by its posting data: reference "withdraw", negative amount, on the account. withdrawnToday sums -Amount of such postings dated ledger.Today; credit postings that happen to carry reference "withdraw" are ignored.

Posting has no kind field, so a debit or transfer whose caller passes reference "withdraw" is indistinguishable from a withdrawal and would count towards the limit. The Posting type was not changed to add a kind (would alter a public record and every construction site).

withdraw checks InvalidAmount, then UnknownAccount (via balance), then InsufficientFunds (balance < amount, matching debit), then DailyLimitExceeded with remaining = 500.00 - withdrawnToday; limit inclusive (withdrawn + amount > 500 refuses).
Limit and reference exposed as named public values Ledger.dailyWithdrawalLimit (500m) and Ledger.withdrawalReference ("withdraw"), the limit being a fixed constant rather than configurable.

Added Store.withdraw that delegates to Ledger.withdraw and shifts the balance cache, so the store (documented as keeping its cache in step with every operation) supports the new operation. Not required by V8.
Business date for 'today' is LedgerState.Today, the same date new postings are stamped with.

Implemented R2 as well as R1, despite the team lead's note that R2 was already done: the existing closePeriod charged 1.00 on any balance >= 1.00 (including premium balances) and the R2 acceptance test fails under that rule. The requirement and its acceptance criteria (all tests pass) take precedence over the note.

periodFee is the single fee rule (0 below 1.00; 1.00 for at least 1.00 and below 1,000.00; 0 for 1,000.00 or more). feeFor is balance |> Result.map periodFee; closePeriod obtains each account's fee via feeFor on the ledger being charged, so all three agree by construction.
