closePeriod posts -fee with reference fee:<periodId> only when fee > 0, and records 0 in Fees for every other account. The idempotence path (ClosedPeriods lookup) is unchanged.
No overdraft check is added at close: periodFee never exceeds the balance (it is non-zero only when the balance is at least 1.00), so charging it cannot overdraw the account.
Fee postings remain distinct from withdrawals (reference fee:<periodId>, not withdraw), so the V8 daily limit is unaffected by period close.

Did not retarget the solution to net8.0 as the team lead asked. The unit's limits forbid changing the target framework or SDK pin, and these rank above the team-lead context. The repository targets net10.0 (Directory.Build.props), global.json pins SDK 10.0.100, and only SDK 10.0.402 is installed, so a net8.0 build could not be verified here anyway.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState field ClosedAccounts: Set<AccountId>, kept disjoint from Accounts; closeAccount moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts. Adding a record field leaves every function signature unchanged. Ledger.empty is the only construction site in the repository; code elsewhere that builds LedgerState with record syntax would need the new field.

closeAccount checks via Ledger.balance, which returns UnknownAccount for an id not in Accounts (never opened or already closed); this check comes first. NonZeroBalance carries the current balance and the check uses <> 0m. Balances can never be negative (no overdrafts), so in practice this means a positive balance.

Unknown-account behaviour after closing follows automatically, because credit, debit, transfer, withdraw, withdrawnToday, feeFor and closePeriod all check against Accounts. openAccount additionally refuses ids in ClosedAccounts with DuplicateAccount.

Added Store.closeAccount, which commits Ledger.closeAccount and removes the id from the store's balance cache, so Store.balance reports UnknownAccount for a closed account (the cache is documented as following every operation). Not required by V1.
Journal order for the account is Ledger.postingsOf id ledger |> List.rev, because LedgerState.Postings is stored newest first. The handoff note saying it is oldest first was rejected.
Postings are tracked by their index in the account's journal, not by value equality, so two identical postings (same date, amount and reference) are distinct and each can be matched at most once.

Day distance is |BookedOn.DayNumber - Date.DayNumber| with a window of 2 days inclusive (named Reconciliation.maxDayGap). The best candidate is chosen by (distance, journal index), which gives closest date first and then the earliest in journal order.
An account that is not open is refused with UnknownAccount, checked against LedgerState.Accounts. Accounts closed under V1 are therefore refused even though their postings remain in the journal.

BankLine and ReconciliationReport were added to Domain.fs exactly as specified, and Reconciliation.fs was added to Ledger.fsproj after Ledger.fs. Parameters are explicitly typed per DOK-FS-001, although the new record labels do not overlap with existing ones.
Ledger.available is implemented here as balance minus the sum of the account's active holds. The team lead's suggested Ledger.availableBalance does not exist.

Active holds are stored as LedgerState.Holds: Map<string, Hold>, keyed by hold id across all accounts, which gives the 'any account' duplicate check. Hold = { HeldAccount; HeldAmount }; its labels deliberately differ from Posting's Account/Amount to avoid the record inference ambiguity in DOK-FS-001. Releasing removes the entry, so the id can be reused; no history of released holds is kept.

placeHold refuses an amount above the available amount; an amount exactly equal to it is accepted. debit and transfer (source) now use available instead of balance in the same InsufficientFunds position, so their other refusals and their order are unchanged. Holds on a transfer's destination are irrelevant.

Ledger.withdraw (V8) also checks funds against available rather than balance, because held money 'cannot be spent' and a cash withdrawal is a spend. V3-R2 names only debit and transfer, while V8-R1 says 'more than the balance', so this resolves a gap between the two requirements. The refusal order is unchanged (InsufficientFunds stays third).
closePeriod and feeFor are unchanged and still use the balance, as R2 requires, so a period fee can take available below zero when holds cover the whole balance.

Added Store.placeHold and Store.releaseHold, which commit the new state and leave the balance cache untouched because holds do not change balances. Store.debit and Store.transfer respect holds through Ledger.debit and Ledger.transfer.

Stopped blocked instead of choosing between DEC-V7-EMPTY-NOOP and DEC-V7-ONE-PAIR. Both are recorded team decisions at the same authority level inside the same requirement, neither is narrower or newer, and picking one would silently override the other team's accepted decision. Under the directives' authority rules this is escalated, not decided by the engineer.

No partial implementation of sweep was committed. Any implementation must give the zero-balance case some behaviour, which would amount to making the decision from U6-D1. The repository is left at the staged state, so the provided V7 acceptance tests do not compile until sweep exists.
Ranking uses Ledger.balance, not Ledger.available: the requirement says 'largest balances', and holds (V3) do not change a balance.

Ties are broken explicitly with String.CompareOrdinal on the id strings in a sortWith comparer, rather than relying on F# structural comparison of AccountId. List.truncate gives the count-0 and count-too-large cases.
'Open accounts' means LedgerState.Accounts, so accounts closed under V1 are excluded.
The negative-count check comes before anything else, so it applies to an empty ledger too.

An order the payer cannot fully cover is not paid at all and is reported as Skipped with the transfer's refusal. Partial payment with a recorded shortfall, as the team-lead context described, was not built. V5-R2 says this choice 'is decided in docs/design/standing-orders.md; follow it', and that accepted note's rule is 'paid in full or not at all'; it lists partial payment as a rejected alternative.

Payment is Ledger.transfer unchanged, so it is all-or-nothing and checks the payer's available amount. Held money (V3) cannot pay a standing order, and closed accounts, SameAccount and similar refusals become Skipped with that error.

Validation goes through the list once in list order with a set of ids already seen, returning the first order with Value <= 0, a DayOfMonth outside 1-31, or a repeated OrderId. Only then is the date applied through Ledger.setDate, which gives DateInPast and moves the business date. A refused run returns the input ledger untouched.

Due logic is exposed as StandingOrders.isDue and uses DateTime.DaysInMonth. The reference is built by StandingOrders.reference with an invariant-culture yyyy-MM-dd format, so it does not depend on the machine's locale. Due orders are sorted with String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId and folded so that each payment sees the earlier ones.
AlreadyPaid is detected by any posting in the journal (any account) with reference standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd>. Skipped orders leave no posting, so a later run for the same date pays them.
No Store.run was added. A run touches several accounts' balances, and the store's balance cache would need per-transfer updates; V5 does not ask for it.
The daily limit is inclusive: withdrawals per account and business date may total exactly 500.00; refusal only when withdrawn + amount > 500.00, with remaining = 500.00 - withdrawn.

A withdrawal is identified by reference 'withdraw', a negative amount and Date = LedgerState.Today; Posting gets no new field. Positive postings with that reference are ignored (assumption); debit/transfer with the literal reference 'withdraw' would count.
Refusal checks run in the required order: InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, InsufficientFunds, DailyLimitExceeded; refusals return Error and change nothing.
Relied on existing Ledger.balance/postingsOf (derived balances) and the private post helper so the withdrawal posting is stamped with LedgerState.Today.
Added Store.withdraw that commits Ledger.withdraw and shifts the balance cache, keeping DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE.
The fee rule exists only in Ledger.periodFee; feeFor = balance mapped through periodFee; closePeriod charges feeFor of each account, so preview and close always agree.
periodFee implements the V4-R2 table: below 1.00 -> 0; at least 1.00 and below 1,000.00 -> 1.00; 1,000.00 or more -> 0.

closePeriod records a fee:<periodId> posting only when the fee is more than 0, lists every account in Fees (0 when none), and keeps its idempotence (a repeated close returns the first summary and records nothing).
feeFor refuses an unopened account with UnknownAccount by reusing Ledger.balance (derived balances); it records nothing.
Store needs no change: it exposes no closePeriod, so its balance cache is unaffected by the fee rule.
Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState.ClosedAccounts: Set<AccountId>, disjoint from Accounts; closeAccount moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts and records no posting.
openAccount refuses an id that is open or in ClosedAccounts with DuplicateAccount, so closed ids are never reused whether or not they had postings.
closeAccount checks via Ledger.balance: UnknownAccount first (never opened or already closed), then NonZeroBalance with the current derived balance; refusals change nothing.

Relied on every existing operation (balance, credit, debit, transfer, closePeriod, withdraw, feeFor) checking membership in LedgerState.Accounts, so removing the id makes it unknown everywhere and excludes it from period close.
Added Store.closeAccount that commits Ledger.closeAccount and removes the id from the balance cache.
Kept the target framework net10.0 and SDK pin 10.0.100; did not retarget to net8.0 as the team lead asked.

Greedy matching over lines in the given order; each line takes the closest-dated unmatched candidate, ties to the earlier posting in journal order; candidates need equal value, exactly equal memo/reference and at most 2 days apart (inclusive).
Postings are tracked by journal position, not structural equality, so identical postings are each matched at most once and independently.
Journal order is Ledger.postingsOf reversed, relying on the accepted newest-first storage of LedgerState.Postings.
An account not in LedgerState.Accounts (never opened or closed) is refused with UnknownAccount; reconcile is a pure read and returns no new ledger state.

Day distance is the absolute difference of DateOnly.DayNumber; the 2-day window is the named constant Reconciliation.maxDaysApart. Reconciliation.fs is a Tier 2 module compiled after Ledger.fs and before Store.fs.

Active holds are stored in LedgerState.Holds: Map<string, Hold> keyed by hold id (Hold = { HoldAccount; HoldAmount }); release removes the entry so the id can be reused; holds record no postings and do not change balance.
Hold fields are named HoldAccount/HoldAmount rather than Account/Amount, to avoid ambiguous F# record inference with Posting.

available = Ledger.balance minus the sum of the account's active holds; placeHold refuses in order InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, DuplicateHold (any account), InsufficientFunds (amount > available); a hold equal to the available amount is allowed.
debit and transfer (source) check the amount against available instead of balance; refusal kinds and order unchanged; closePeriod and feeFor still use balance.
withdraw still checks funds against the balance (V8-R1 wording), so held money can be withdrawn as cash.
closeAccount ignores holds (checks balance only); holds on a closed account remain until released.
Added Store.placeHold and Store.releaseHold; they update the journal state only, since holds do not change balances, so the balance cache needs no change.

Did not implement sweep and did not choose between DEC-V7-EMPTY-NOOP and DEC-V7-ONE-PAIR; the conflict needs Operations and Audit (the decision owners) to resolve it in requirements/V7.md and contracts/V7.json.
richest ranks by Ledger.balance (derived from postings), not Ledger.available, so active holds do not change the ranking.
Only accounts in LedgerState.Accounts take part, so closed accounts (ClosedAccounts) are excluded; zero-balance open accounts are included.
Ties are ordered with String.CompareOrdinal on the AccountId string, ascending; order is balance descending first.
A negative count is refused with the new InvalidCount case before anything else; count 0 gives Ok [] and a count above the number of open accounts returns all of them (List.truncate).

An order the payer cannot cover is paid in full or not at all: one Ledger.transfer of the whole Value; a refusal is reported as Skipped (id, error) and nothing is moved or recorded. The team lead's partial-payment-with-shortfall instruction was not followed.
run validates every order in list order (Value <= 0, DayOfMonth outside 1-31, repeated OrderId) before checking the date, then reuses Ledger.setDate for the DateInPast refusal and the date move.
Due rule: DayOfMonth = date.Day, or DayOfMonth > date.Day and date is the last day of its month (date.AddDays(1).Day = 1), which avoids DateTime APIs in Tier 2.

Due orders are sorted with String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId and paid in a fold so each payment sees earlier ones; the reference is standing:<OrderId>:<yyyy-MM-dd> formatted with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture.
AlreadyPaid is decided by any posting in the whole journal carrying the order's dated reference; skipped orders leave no such posting and are paid on a later run for the same date.
Payments go through Ledger.transfer, so the V3 rule applies: held money cannot pay an order (Skipped with InsufficientFunds), and closed payer/payee accounts are skipped as UnknownAccount.
StandingOrders.fs is a Tier 2 module compiled after Reconciliation.fs and before Store.fs; no Store wrapper was added (the requirement names only StandingOrders.run).

The daily limit is inclusive: refuse only when today's withdrawals plus amount exceed 500.00; DailyLimitExceeded carries 500.00 minus today's withdrawals. Refusal order: InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, InsufficientFunds (amount > balance; withdrawing the whole balance is allowed), DailyLimitExceeded.

A withdrawal is identified only by reference 'withdraw' on the account's postings dated LedgerState.Today; withdrawnToday is derived from postings (no stored counter). A debit called with reference 'withdraw' would be counted; Posting was not extended.
Added Store.withdraw that commits via Ledger.withdraw and shifts the balance cache, keeping DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE true for the new operation.
Reused the existing balance and private post helpers and the newest-first postingsOf helper; limit and reference are public constants Ledger.dailyWithdrawalLimit and Ledger.withdrawalReference.

The fee rule lives only in public Ledger.periodFee (below 1.00 -> 0; 1.00 to below 1,000.00 -> 1.00; 1,000.00 or more -> 0; threshold Ledger.premiumBalanceThreshold). feeFor = balance mapped through periodFee (UnknownAccount for an account not open); closePeriod charges periodFee of each balance.
closePeriod posts a fee:<periodId> posting of minus the fee only when the fee is more than 0; the summary's Fees lists every account (0 when none); idempotence per period id unchanged.
Rejected the team lead's note that R2 was already implemented and verified, and implemented R2 in this unit.
feeFor is built on the existing Ledger.balance (derived from postings), and Store was not changed: Store has no closePeriod, so DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE is unaffected.

Closed accounts are remembered in a new LedgerState.ClosedAccounts set, disjoint from Accounts; closeAccount moves the id from Accounts to ClosedAccounts, openAccount refuses an id in either set with DuplicateAccount. Since balance, credit, debit, transfer, withdraw, feeFor and closePeriod all work from Accounts, a closed account is unknown to them and is neither charged nor listed by a period close. No existing function signature changed.

closeAccount is built on Ledger.balance (derived from postings): UnknownAccount first, then any balance <> 0 is refused with NonZeroBalance(id, balance); closing records no posting and leaves the journal unchanged.
Added Store.closeAccount that commits via Ledger.closeAccount and removes the id from the balance cache, keeping DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE true.
Did not retarget to net8.0 as the team lead asked; target framework net10.0 and SDK pin 10.0.100 stay unchanged.

Greedy matching in line order: a line's candidates are unmatched postings of the account with Amount = Value, Reference = Memo (ordinal, case-sensitive) and |Date.DayNumber - BookedOn.DayNumber| <= 2 (Reconciliation.matchWindowDays); it takes the candidate minimising (day distance, journal position), so ties go to the earlier posting. No global optimal assignment.

Journal order comes from Ledger.postings (oldest first) filtered to the account, not LedgerState.Postings, which is stored newest first (DEC-BASE-NEWEST-FIRST kept). reconcile only reads the ledger and refuses an id not in LedgerState.Accounts (never opened or closed) with UnknownAccount.

BankLine and ReconciliationReport added to Domain.fs exactly as specified; Reconciliation.fs is a pure Tier 2 module compiled after Ledger.fs and before Store.fs; Store unchanged since reconciliation records nothing. No existing public signature changed.

Active holds are stored in a new LedgerState.Holds: Map<string, Hold> keyed by hold id, Hold = { OnAccount: AccountId; Held: decimal } (field names distinct from Posting's to avoid record-inference ambiguity, DOK-FS-001). releaseHold removes the entry, so a released id may be reused. Holds record no postings and never change balance; no stored balance added.

Ledger.available = Ledger.balance minus the sum of the account's active holds (UnknownAccount for an account not open, closed included). placeHold refusal order: InvalidAmount, UnknownAccount, DuplicateHold (any account), InsufficientFunds when amount > available; a hold of exactly the available amount is allowed.
debit and transfer (source only) refuse with InsufficientFunds when amount > available instead of amount > balance; other refusals and their order unchanged; closePeriod unchanged (fee by balance).

withdraw also checks InsufficientFunds against the available amount (held money cannot be withdrawn as cash). The requirement names only debit and transfer; this extends 'Money that is held cannot be spent' to withdraw. Behaviour with no holds is identical, so V8 is unaffected.
Added Store.placeHold and Store.releaseHold committing via Ledger; the balance cache is untouched because holds change no balance, keeping DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE true.

Stopped blocked without implementing sweep, because Ordo contract admission reported ORDO.CONTRACT.UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT for CONFLICT-V7-EMPTY-SWEEP; did not pick either team's decision, since choosing one would silently reverse the other team's recorded decision.

Ledger.richest ranks open accounts (LedgerState.Accounts, so closed accounts are excluded and zero-balance open accounts take part) by Ledger.balance derived from postings, not by Ledger.available; holds do not lower the reported amount.

Order is balance descending then account id string ascending via String.CompareOrdinal; the sorted list is truncated to count (0 -> [], larger count -> all open accounts). A negative count is refused with the new LedgerError case InvalidCount count before the ledger is read.

Store was not changed: richest only reads the ledger and records nothing, so DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE is unaffected. No existing public signature changed; InvalidCount is appended as the last LedgerError case.

Inside richest, balance is called only for ids taken from LedgerState.Accounts, so it is always Ok; Result.defaultValue 0m is used, following the existing closePeriod pattern, rather than duplicating the balance sum.

A due order is paid with one Ledger.transfer of its full Value; a refused transfer (InsufficientFunds against available included) moves nothing and gives Skipped(id, error). No partial payment or shortfall record, keeping DEC-V5-PAID-IN-FULL. The team lead's instruction to pay what the payer holds and record the shortfall was not followed.

Validation walks orders in list order and refuses the first with Value <= 0, DayOfMonth outside 1..31 or an id already seen earlier, with InvalidOrder id; only then is the date checked and moved via Ledger.setDate (DateInPast for an earlier date; the current date is allowed). InvalidOrder is appended as the last LedgerError case; StandingOrder and OrderOutcome added to Domain.fs as specified.

Due-ness is the public StandingOrders.isDue: DayOfMonth = date.Day, or DayOfMonth > DateTime.DaysInMonth and date is the month's last day. Due orders are sorted by String.CompareOrdinal on OrderId and folded so each sees earlier payments. The reference is the public StandingOrders.reference, 'standing:<OrderId>:' + date formatted yyyy-MM-dd with the invariant culture.

AlreadyPaid is decided by any posting in LedgerState.Postings carrying the order's reference for that date (not restricted to payer/payee); such an order records nothing. A skipped order has no posting, so a later same-date run pays it.

StandingOrders.fs is a pure Tier 2 module compiled after Ledger.fs and before Reconciliation.fs/Store.fs. Store was not changed because the requirement names no Store operation, so DEC-BASE-STORE-CACHE is unaffected. No existing public signature changed.
